name: TX-14
label: Likely R

key_factors: Strong Republican district lean of about 12 points
Incumbent Randy Weber running with a large cash advantage
Democrat Thurman Bartie has raised almost nothing and is out of cash
Prediction markets price Weber near 95% to win
model.rationale: The district's Republican lean, Weber's incumbency and roughly $920,000 on hand against Bartie's near-zero war chest all point the same direction, and Polymarket gives Bartie only about a 6% chance. With no polls or expert ratings available, the forecast stays close to the fundamentals-based estimate of a mid-teens Republican margin.
model.watch: Any late polling or a surge in Democratic outside spending would be the first sign the race is closer than the money and district lean suggest.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Randy Weber seeks another term in this southeast Texas district, which leans about 12 points Republican at baseline. He enters the general election renominated, with roughly $920,000 in cash and modest outside support, and no recorded opposition spending against him. No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, so the picture rests on fundamentals and market pricing.

Democrat Thurman Bartie has raised only about $27,000 and reports negative cash on hand, leaving little capacity to introduce himself to voters. Prediction markets give Weber roughly a 95% chance of winning. The expected margin is a mid-teens Republican win, with meaningful but limited uncertainty given the absence of polling.
